assertion.statement: The two induced Dirichlet characters in C4 are equal if their values agree at every common good prime.
assertion.objects: The two finite-order Dirichlet characters compared in the coefficient-conjugate newform argument at anchor line31.
assertion.hypotheses: Both characters factor through a common finite abelian quotient; their values at every prime outside the finite bad set agree, as supplied by the displayed coefficient formula.
assertion.quantifiers: For the two actual characters and all elements of their common finite quotient.
assertion.parameter_range: The fixed levels and character moduli in C4; primes outside their finite bad set.
assertion.uniformity: Only equality for this pair; no field, level or coefficient enlargement is inferred.
assertion.constants: No effective prime bound or quantitative estimate.
assertion.normalizations: Character value at a good prime equals its value on arithmetic Frobenius.
assertion.exceptional_cases: The coefficient identity and same-form/primitive-source hypotheses are retained inputs. The Euler-factor formula and semisimple trace lemma are not premises.
assertion.limit_order: Fix the common finite abelian quotient; apply density outside the bad set; deduce equality on every quotient element.

use.reason: Factor both Dirichlet characters through the Galois group of a common cyclotomic extension. For each element choose a good prime with that Frobenius using finite-abelian density. The already established equality at that prime gives equality on the chosen element. This proves character equality without using the conditional Euler formula or semisimple representation theory.

supplier.statement: For a finite abelian extension of number fields, every element of its Galois group occurs as Frobenius at unramified primes outside any fixed finite excluded set.
